hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text: We had the absolute best experience chatting with and getting to know Meline and her manager Gabin at the OA Bar! They are both so much fun to talk to and get to know they made our experience even better than we've already had! We also wanted to recognize Hughes at the pool bar with his quick service and great attitude!

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text: We spent 4 night at the Westin in Bora Bora as part of our honey moon trip. We can't say but positive words about our stay here: the place and atmosphere are idyllic and the staff is exceptionally profesional. We would like to commend Mirabelle in particular, who has served us during our dinners at Tipanier restaurant with an extraordinary level of kindness and attention to the smallest detail to ensure we were completely at ease. So thanks to the whole staff for making us feel such a great time during our honey moon, we wish we will ever have the opportunity to come back again in the future.
review_title: Perfect time during our honey moon trip

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text: The Westin Bora Bora is not very guest friendly. The managers and concierge give wrong or incomplete answers to questions. We were denied a late checkout. We had to be out of the room at 12 and then wait 5 hours for the boat to the airport. We were not offered a transit room or guest villa for the 5 hours. We were told Bonvoy members could not get a late checkout because the hotel was fully booked even though the villas on either side of us have been empty for the last 6 days. There is no water in the villa. They give you a thermos at the airport and you have to fill it up at a water/ice station. The water tastes terrible. The concierge told us there eould be water and towels on the boat we rented - wrong. The operator of the boat company did a tsk tsk when we told them what we we told. She felt sorry for us and gave us 2 bottles of water. The resort is very pretty but they make you feel like cattle. I was even reprimanded by the server at the pool bar for what he thought was an inadaquate tip.
review_title: Beautiful resort. Friendly staff. Unpleasant management.

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text: We absolutely loved our stay at The Westin Bora Bora. Waking up in our overwater villa with those incredible lagoon and Mount Otemanu views was unforgettable. The staff were so friendly and helpful, and everything felt perfect from start to finish. Definitely one of the most beautiful places we've ever stayed!
review_title: A Dream Stay in Bora Bora 💙

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text: Location is everything - and the Westin Bora Bora does not disappoint as it located right in front of Mt Otemanu with the bluest of blue lagoons. I thought solo travel would be weird - anything but! Property is beautiful with plenty of places to find a quiet spot to simply chill as well as your room/balcony. The Spa was out of this world - services are great & you can easily add another hour or 2 enjoying the steam room and plunge pool. Heaven. All the staff was welcoming and attentive: the Polynesian night is a must. It's a little confusing what you can book on line/What's App vs need to go to the concierge for. Food is good - but a little mundane for the price; but the portions are huge. This is FRENCH Polynesia - would have loved to seen more French and Island specialties (or something like CoCo Beach on Moorea). I liked that half potions were an option for may dishes (except dessert - also huge portions!). At the 'O'A the "tapas" we too big and wished they had smaller portions - ordered 2 that dinner. Maere is the highlight for foodies - book well before you arrive in Bora Bora as seating is very limited. The hidden gem is Honu Tiki....afternoon bliss. Eco Center is great - but only one turtle. :-( My only disappoint for a resort of this caliber was the coffee, lattes & cappuccinos, were horrible - its push the button from an industrial machine (think airport lounge). They need a cool stand alone coffee area with a real espresso machine (had the BEST in Papeete) for iced lattes, matcha and some yummy (small) snacks....! This property is a GREAT place to stay to relax - often for once in a lifetime trip!

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text: We loved our stay at The Westin! I liked the hotel a lot, the customer service was wonderful, and the views are simply spectacular. An incredible experience that I would repeat without a doubt. Totally recommended!

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text: We just left the Westin after an unforgettable four-night stay. The location of this brand-new resort is arguably the best in the island, topping their competitors. It is hard to miss the picture perfect view of Otemanu everywhere in the resort, but the never-crowded beach and enormous pool add to the magical beauty of the place. The rooms were spacious and spotless, with jawdropping views. The grounds were impeccable, well-thought out, and designed. The food ranged from adequate to great, and far better than we expected, and always situated in beautiful, calm settings. The bicycles all over the resort became an event unto itself—we loved just biking from our room to the main facilities and back! But really the most indelible part of this stay was the hospitality and service. We can truly say that the Westin team went above and beyond to make our family so well cared for. There was a consistent high level of service, from the warm welcome upon arrival by Manon to the rock star concierge team of Alexandra, Leilani, and Sebastien, to Maxime, Hinatea, and all the staff at the restaurants, to the countless warm smiles and 'ia ora nas from any Westin groundsperson, bartender, transport, and housekeeping staff we saw (and there were many!). This is clearly a very well-run and trained team, and it is so difficult to maintain such a high level of service and hospitality across dining, housekeeping, concierge, front desk, and transportation to have it run so seamlessly, so consistently, that it deserves special mention.
review_title: World-class hospitality, stunning location, and amazing facilities

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text: We had an amazing stay at The Westin Bora Bora! The whole island is unlike anywhere we have ever been. A special shoutout to our friend Alan, who works at the resort! He went above and beyond to make us feel welcome and made our time in Bora Bora even more memorable. It's the people who can really make a great trip special, and Alan definitely did that for us.

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text: This was the most beautiful resort we've ever stayed at! The service everywhere was top notch. Everyday we were on the beach or at the pool we got the best service. Alan was incredible at taking care of us. He was our favorite person on the resort. Our family had the best time and every time we walked by or saw Alan he would make a point to talk to us and make sure we were having a good time! The drinks are so good! Don't miss out on the Mai Tais if you go! So good. Can't recommend this place enough!

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text: Subtracting 1 star for food being meh and overpriced. ROOM: Our room was beautiful, and housekeeper did a great job. AMENITIES: The amenities are absolutely gorgeous, including airport transport, kayaks, paddle boards, bicycles, and a nice gym. SPA: The spa prices were absolutely astronomical - $250 per person for one hour, versus about $120 in San Diego for 90 minutes. We refused to book anything at that price. TURTLE DISCOVERY: overpriced ($70 per person for a 1 hour presentation), and they only have one turtle right now. Maere (the upscale dining restaurant): I specifically notated that I was pregnant (no raw fish) and my husband has a mushroom allergy. By the first course, they served my husband mushrooms; they apologized, but within 30 minutes he became violently ill and vomited for 20 minutes straight - we suspect food poisoning, and lost an entire day of our trip, cancelling our reservation at what I hear is the best restaurant on the island. Te Ava (swim-up bar): probably the best food at the resort, though they brought us the wrong drink more than once. Tippanier breakfast buffet: the only egg option one day was extremely runny scrambled eggs; we later learned there IS an omelette bar but the waiter has to be asked. Dinner-with-show was $160/person and underwhelming for the quality/options as a pregnant guest who couldn't eat much fish. SERVICE OVERALL: everyone was super nice, but after food is served they don't check on you enough - at $1,800/night you shouldn't have to flag someone down for the check at every meal.

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text:
I'm finally getting around to writing this review after my stay there last year. I can only hope the many issues my wife and I faced have been corrected and that people don't read weirdly biased reviews on here and elsewhere and expect a 10/10 experience. Here was our experience:

The Westin Bora Bora is a beautiful property with genuinely friendly staff who try to remember your name. However, for a resort operating at this price point and marketing a luxury experience, the reality fell vastly short. The stay was defined by basic service breakdowns, severe communication issues, and unacceptable neglect.

Arrival & Concierge Logistics
Subpar Arrival Experience: Upon landing, while guests heading to nearby luxury properties (like the St. Regis) were immediately greeted with leis and seamless transfers, Westin guests were left waiting 20 minutes just for staff to appear at the airport desk. We were then made to sit on the transfer boat for nearly an hour before finally departing for the resort. If you read other reviews, you'll see this is apparently a common experience for Westin guests.

Dismissive Concierge Service: Prior to arrival, I sent multiple emails to our assigned concierge contact (Lucile) regarding dinner reservations and received zero response. This forced us to spend vacation time organizing dining upon arrival. Worse, when I asked the concierge for help arranging boat transport to a well known off property restaurant, I was told they didn't have a boat that could reach it and was literally advised to "Google for boats" myself. For a luxury resort concierge, telling a guest to Google basic local logistics is baffling.

Excursion & Spa Mismanagement: A promised follow up on a joint fishing trip to give us details on pricing and timing never happened. I had to call directly to find out we were already booked. Additionally, a spa appointment was arbitrarily canceled an hour after booking and moved to a different time with a completely different treatment.

Housekeeping & Basic Essentials
The Toilet Paper & Cleaning Struggle: Daily housekeeping was unacceptably negligent. Our room went completely unserviced for three days. I had to call three separate times (being promised each time that it would be taken care of) and ultimately had to escalate the issue to the General Manager, Caesar, just to get our room cleaned and receive basic necessities like toilet paper and coffee pods. In speaking with other guests on property, several were experiencing the exact same basic shortages.

Bizarre Housekeeping Interactions: Housekeeping showed up at 8:00 PM one evening claiming they couldn't service the room earlier because my wallet had been left on the counter the day before (and noted they had taken a photograph of it). This was a bizarre interaction, and it remains unclear why a wallet on a counter precluded servicing the room. Even after the room was finally cleaned, empty toilet paper rolls were left sitting on bathroom shelves, a pillow was left without a pillowcase, and basic amenities like washcloths were hit or miss.

Food, Beverage & Amenities
Dining Service & Quality Breakdown: Breakfast service was chaotic and slow. On our first day, we waited 20 minutes just for water, coffee arrived late or incorrect, and basic menu items like syrup and pineapple for French toast were completely out of stock by 9:30 AM. I only learned of the missing items after receiving a plain piece of dry French toast with powdered sugar and having to ask where the rest of the meal was. On our second night, we were served raw, undercooked potatoes at dinner. Simple requests like ice water at the beach cabana went unfulfilled.

Oa Bar Experience: Service at the Oa Bar was consistently sluggish. One evening during happy hour, I sat for 20 minutes with an empty glass. When a server finally came over, it was 5 minutes past the happy hour cutoff. He gave me an attitude when I tried to order and acted like he was doing me a favor by honoring the happy hour price for that round, despite the delay being entirely on their end.

Unfulfilled Promises & Room Issues: Reusable water bottles, which are a highlighted selling point in marketing materials, were out of stock upon arrival with no advance notice or mention at check in (though two mysteriously appeared days later in our room). An upgrade promised for Day 3 required chasing down management to receive it for just our final night. Additionally, the WC and closet suffered from intense dampness, leaving our clothes smelling stale.

Property Grounds
Neglected Bike Fleet: Many guest bicycles across the property were in terrible condition with flat tires, broken handlebars, broken chains, and damaged seats. This led guests to hoard the few functional bikes at their private villas.

Rule Enforcement: Guests were permitted to smoke on the docks directly in front of concierge staff, despite property rules strictly prohibiting it.

Some Good Notes
Fishing: The deep sea fishing trip was amazing (though it was operated by a 3rd party). We caught a big Wahoo fish, and the chef at the property offered to prepare it as sashimi and grill the rest for us. It was easily the best meal I had there. Maybe I'm biased because I caught the fish...or maybe the bar is super low because the other meals just weren't that great.

Staff Friendliness: The staff were super friendly, especially those at the pool. They remembered our names and always greeted us with a warm smile.

Beautiful Resort: It is Bora Bora, so the natural beauty of the property and lagoon itself is stunning.

Summary
While individual staff members were warm and welcoming, the Westin Bora Bora is currently suffering from major operational and management failures. When a guest has to call three times and speak directly to the GM just to get toilet paper, and is told to "Google it" by the concierge, it is simply not operating as a luxury resort. I suggest spending a little more money or points to stay at neighboring properties like the St. Regis instead.

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text:
We stayed five nights at The Westin Bora Bora, and honestly, it couldn't have been better. We travel extensively, so we've experienced some of the world's finest luxury hotels and destinations. We have a pretty good understanding of what defines a true luxury vacation, and The Westin Bora Bora absolutely delivers.

From the moment we landed in Bora Bora at 8:15 am, everything was seamless. The sweetest Westin representative was waiting for us at the airport with beautiful leis and refillable water bottles. After collecting our luggage, someone immediately took care of our bags, and within minutes we were comfortably seated on the hotel's boat for the 25 minute ride across the lagoon.

Arriving at the resort was unforgettable. The first view of the property with Mount Otemanu rising behind it literally took our breath away. In our opinion, The Westin has the best view of Mount Otemanu in all of Bora Bora. We've seen the other resorts from the water, and none of them offer the same perfectly centered view. It is simply spectacular.

Check-in was smooth and efficient. Emma was incredibly warm and welcoming, making us feel at home immediately. I've seen reviews mentioning long check-in waits, but I honestly don't think that's the hotel's fault. We arrived early in the morning, so there was absolutely no wait to check in. The entire check-in process itself took about 15 minutes, which is completely reasonable considering all the information provided and the warm welcome. When we checked out around 1 pm, about 16 people happened to arrive at the same time. Naturally, there will be a short wait when that many guests arrive all at once. Even then, you're in one of the most beautiful places on Earth, relaxing with a refreshing welcome juice and a cold towel while taking in the incredible scenery. It's hardly something worth complaining about.

As part of check-in, you're also given a beach bag, which quickly becomes your go to bag around the resort and you'll notice almost every guest carrying one!
Afterward, Sébastien gave us a wonderful tour of the property. Since we had arrived so early and the resort was completely full, our room wasn't quite ready yet, which was completely understandable. We simply changed into our swimsuits and headed straight to the beach to start enjoying paradise.

When we finally got to our overwater bungalow, it exceeded every expectation. The bungalow was immaculate, looked brand new, and was beautifully designed. Every detail was spotless and perfectly maintained. Stepping onto our deck each morning and looking out over the crystal clear turquoise lagoon was simply magical. The view was absolutely out of this world and one we'll never forget.

Another complaint I'd read before arriving was about the bicycles supposedly being broken or unavailable. That couldn't have been further from our experience. There were bikes everywhere. Honestly, it felt like there were more bikes than guests! We never once had trouble finding one, and they were a fantastic way to get around the beautiful resort. We absolutely loved biking everywhere. It's such a fun and relaxing way to explore the property, and it became part of our daily routine.

We also took advantage of the complimentary kayaks, which were another highlight of our stay. Paddling through the crystal clear lagoon while surrounded by the incredible scenery was an unforgettable experience.

The food throughout our stay was also excellent. We especially loved the breakfast buffet, which had an incredible variety of options. Whether you wanted fresh tropical fruit, pastries, made-to-order eggs, local specialties, or a more traditional breakfast, there was truly something for everyone. But what made breakfast even more memorable was the setting. Sitting by the beautiful inner lagoon while enjoying our meal and watching blacktip reef sharks and gracefully swim by was an experience we'll never forget.

Lunch was another highlight because we loved having it delivered directly to our beach cabana instead of having to leave the beach to sit in the restaurant. It was such a relaxing luxury to enjoy delicious food while soaking up the incredible views.
Dinner each evening was equally wonderful, especially as we watched the breathtaking Bora Bora sunsets. Between the outstanding food and the spectacular scenery, every meal felt like a special occasion.

We've been fortunate enough to travel to approximately 60 countries, including two trips to the Maldives. People often compare Bora Bora to the Maldives because of the overwater bungalows and crystal clear lagoons. While they certainly share those similarities, what truly sets Bora Bora apart is Mount Otemanu. No photograph can prepare you for seeing it in person. The mountain creates one of the most dramatic and breathtaking landscapes we've ever experienced, making Bora Bora unlike anywhere else in the world.

What also makes The Westin so special is its people. Every single employee we encountered was genuinely kind, welcoming, and always greeted us with a smile and a cheerful "Ia Orana." Their warmth and hospitality made us feel like valued guests throughout our stay. Luxury isn't just about beautiful rooms and stunning scenery, it's about how people make you feel, and the staff at The Westin excelled in every way.

We can confidently say that Bora Bora has become our favorite place on Earth, and The Westin made that experience unforgettable. If you're looking for breathtaking scenery, impeccable service, genuine hospitality, outstanding food, luxurious accommodations, and a true luxury escape, look no further. We would return in a heartbeat and recommend The Westin Bora Bora without hesitation.
review_title: A Perfect 5 Night Stay at The Westin Bora Bora

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text:
Our family of six stayed at The Westin Bora Bora in three overwater bungalows, and it exceeded every expectation. Before we even arrived, we were surprised with complimentary upgrades to larger overwater villas, each with its own private pool and breathtaking views of Mount Otemanu. It was the perfect start to what became the best vacation our family has ever taken.

The resort itself is absolutely stunning, but what truly sets it apart is the exceptional staff. Every team member was warm, genuine, and incredibly attentive. They quickly learned our family by room number, remembered our names, our food preferences, and always had breakfast and dinner tables perfectly set up for all six of us without us ever having to ask.

The thoughtful touches throughout our stay made us feel truly special. We were welcomed with champagne, nuts, and treats in each of our three villas, and every day we returned to delightful surprises like chocolates, granola bars, and delicious coconut cookies waiting in our rooms.

The property is immaculate. The beach is pristine, the water is unbelievable, and the fitness center is one of the nicest hotel gyms we've ever seen. We especially enjoyed the morning yoga classes overlooking paradise.

There were also so many complimentary activities included that kept everyone entertained: kayaking, paddleboarding, wine tasting, rum tasting, flower crown making, basket weaving, and more. It was the perfect balance of relaxation and authentic Polynesian experiences.

Everything about our stay—from the luxurious accommodations to the flawless service and incredible attention to detail—was simply outstanding. We've been fortunate to travel to many beautiful places around the world, but The Westin Bora Bora stands above them all.

Without question, this was the best family vacation we've ever had, and we cannot wait to return.

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text:
We had an incredible stay at The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa. The resort is absolutely beautiful, with breathtaking views, outstanding facilities, and exceptional service throughout our visit.

A special thank you to Alan at the pool bar. He was amazing—friendly, attentive, and always made us feel welcome. His outstanding service and positive attitude made our time by the pool even more enjoyable.

We would also like to recognize Victorine, our waitress at Varavara and the breakfast buffet. She was warm, professional, and provided exceptional service with a genuine smile. She made every meal a wonderful experience.

A heartfelt thank you as well to Dragan, whose kindness, professionalism, and attention to detail made us feel truly valued throughout our stay.

The breakfast buffet staff were absolutely amazing. Every morning they greeted us warmly and ensured everything was perfect. Their hospitality made each day start on the best possible note.

Thank you to the entire Westin Bora Bora team for making our vacation so memorable. We can't wait to return!
review_title: An Amazing Stay at The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text: We decided to spend 5 nights at the Westin and were really looking forward to the experience. We were very quickly disappointed to see that there is virtually no marine life in the bay, except for sea urchins! What is the point of a bungalow with a window over water, if there is no coral and no fish? Diner at Tipanier, their mid-range restaurant, also did not deliver, with a small piece of duck with an even smaller amount of puree for $63, pretty outrageous even though we knew everything was expensive on the motu. Unfortunately, a day into our trip, unusual circumstances required us to shorten our stay, so we asked management if they could kindly refund two or three nights and we were met with complete indifference and told that "this would affect their bottom line, so it was not possible". I would have expected a much different answer from such a high end hotel, I can therefore not recommend it to anyone.
review_title: No snorkeling and poor management attitude.

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text:
One of the most beautiful stays of my life, the resort is exceptional, the location is incredible in front of the
Otemanu Mountain.
The resort has been recently renovated so everything is new and beautiful. The staff is lovely, thanks to Charlotte Hélène for your warm welcome and kindness.
The rooms are very beautiful, the activities are heavenly.
The restaurants complement each other and you will eat very well.
I recommend it +++ with my eyes closed.

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text:
We stayed at one of the Otemanu overwater villas which was truly magical! The views from the villa were absolutely amazing!

Even though the resort is big and has many villas it felt really private and exclusive at all times. The meals were excellent, with the Maere restaurant being the highlight of the stay. The chef crafts delicious surprise dinner menus for every evening.

We enjoyed the beautiful lagoon by kayak and paddleboard, as well as biking around the islands was amazing.

The Westin's Eco Center also cares for injured turtles that they rehabilitate and release to the wild when possible.

The rooms are spaceous and well equipped, giving wide ocean and Otemanu views directly from the bed.

We definitely had a wonderful stay and hoping to return soon!
review_title: Paradisiac getaway at the newly renovated Westin Bora Bora!

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text:
The Westin Bora Bora was incredible! My husband and I knew we wanted to come here for our 20th anniversary and it didn't disappoint! The overwater bungalows are stunning, the staff is so friendly and attentive to anything you need and they helped make our anniversary beyond anything we could have expected. We had a private beach dinner that was so romantic and they made a gorgeous re-creation of our wedding cake. We were blown away. Lucille and her team created a magical night for us. Niuti was such a fun bartender and was great with the daily rum or wine tastings. The daily activities were so fun. The food was better than we expected. We were so, so sad to leave. As
lifetime platinum members who stay at Marriotts around the world, this is one of the best resorts we've ever experienced. The attention to detail was unmatched. Thank you for making our 20th anniversary so special.

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text:
Stay booked for our honeymoon. A stunning resort, and the true wealth is the kindness of the staff, the extremely high standards, and the beauty of the place, which has a view of nature and eco-responsibility.

A huge thank you to Sebastien from the Guest Relations team, who, with his professionalism, kindness, and passion for the job, made our stay magnificent.

Thanks also to all the staff!
review_title: The true luxury is the view and the kindness of the staff.

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text:
We had a wonderful family trip to the Westin in Bora Bora. We stayed in a 2-bedroom Villa on the lagoon beach area. It was very private, had ample outdoor space with plunge pool. We selected the Westin as we knew it was entirely brand new and 100% glad we made that decision. Rooms were clean, ample outlet options and the decor was very light and refreshing.

What truly was the best - the staff at the Westin. All the workers whether they are international borders or stay on site, or local Tahitian from the mainland of Bora Bora - all of them were so kind throughout our stay. Arthur gave us a great tour right after we checked in and got us situated with all our questions. Lucile was fantastic with food options as we have a few allergies in our family. Florie served us breakfast a few days. I wish I could remember all the servers, waitresses and housekeeping names - as all were great during our stay.

We did jet skis, spa, kayaked lagoon, booked a boat tour of the Lagoon and rented a car one day on mainland of Bora Bora to explore. Concierge was helpful in arranging everything. Boat to/from airport is super easy, and they handle all your luggage and coordinate with your flight times.

Yes - bring your wallet. Food is very expensive. I do wish the restaurants had more variety. Tipanier is closed 2 nights a week for Poly Show (which we didn't do). Maere is a "set tasting menu" only a few nights a week. Due to having the boys we elected not to do. We dined at Varavara several nights and for lunches. It is good, just after 3-4 days you are looking for more options.

I hope to one day return and stay at the Westin again. Thank you to the team of people making that resort a fantastic experience for our family!

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text:
This was one of the best resorts we have ever stayed at.

We stayed 7 nights. We are lifetime platinum with Marriott and used NUAs. The NUA cleared from a base level bungalow to a premium overwater Mountain View with plunge pool villa. They cleared at exactly 5 days.

Arrival- we had no issue and were presented with water bottles at the airport. It took a few minutes to get our luggage and checked in and it's a 20 minute boat ride to the resort but the process was seamless

Check in- check in was great and we got a fantastic tour

Room- our upgraded room was the best room we have ever had. The plunge pool was much needed with the windy weather but the room had housekeeping and turndown service and the espresso machine was great. They did frequently forget to leave us beach towels to use on the deck. We loved the room and spent most of our time here!

Food:
Tipanier- breakfast started to get stale at 7 days, some things rotated (juices and pastries) but most was the same.

For dinner we ate twice and I had the linguine (super heavy but good) and my husband had the Mahi (says it was great, I'm allergic). The second time we both had the tenderloin and it was solid. Mana was our server both nights and he was amazing. Made the meals extra special.

Varavare- we ate here 5 nights. The food was fantastic. We loved the ribeye, pizzas, pastas and nightly specials. The food was pretty solid, I have food allergies, and they made me feel safe.

While repeatedly noted it was my birthday, no one acknowledged it on the day of, we went back two days later and our previous servers remembered it and inquired about it and brought out desert and apologized to make it special a few days later. A huge shoutout to Ani and Moetata who made up for the previous bad experience. They served us several nights and remembered our preferences and made up for bad service on my birthday. They are absolute gems.

Pool bar- we had pizzas and burgers here which were great

Maere- we never ate here as I have food allergies and when asking repeatedly from the manager (starting weeks ahead of trip and continuing during our trip) if it would be doable the response was "it will be fine" but when asked what the alternative menu would look like (did not want to pay premium prices for a vegetarian menu when I am not a vegetarian) I did not get a real answer. When the meal price is $140 per person and you are allergic to most things but they say they can make accommodations (but won't tell you what they would be) it's hard to justify. This is probably the only sore spot on our trip.

Bars:

The French and Italian wine selections are extensive and we truly appreciated this as we are big wine drinkers.

We went to O'A most nights and cannot say enough good things about Quintin the bar manager. He made great recommendations and was always willing to answer questions. He took great photos for us (much needed when traveling as a couple) and made the trip extra special.

On site activities:

Turtles- we did the turtle experience and it was a thousand percent worth it just to support the turtles. We did later see turtles under other bungalows

Paddle boards- we attempted to paddle board a could have days but bad weather prevailed. We were finally able to do so but the winds got bad and we were summoned back after 30 minutes. You can't control Mother Nature but appreciated they stopped us from going out into bad conditions!

Wine/ Rum tasting- we attended both. The wine tasting was a pineapple and those tasting. Both local and was a fun experience even though not our preferred taste. The rum tasting was a light and dark rum and fun experience

Cabanas- we were able to get a cabana late morning when we had down time. They absolutely patrol the pool and prevent the normal "chair game" which we appreciated

Excursions:

We did jet skis and snorkeling through an outside vendor (half the price) but they were able to come pick us up at the resort with no problem! We forgot to carry cash on one of the excursions and we were able to leave a tip with our concierge for him.

All in all the resort was amazing and e have very high standards. As someone with food allergies, that was the only place I feel like communication was scary.

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text: From arrival to departure, every detail was flawless. Outstanding staff, great dining, and unforgettable memories.

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text:
We had a memorable stay at the resort, but it could and should have been so much better.

The Westin Bora Bora was the “newest” resort on the island, the former Le Méridien Bora Bora having been taken over by Marriott/Bonvoy and extensively renovated. It had been reopened not quite 1 year earlier, in September 2024. Our expectations were accordingly quite numerous and high. Unfortunately the resort did not live up to all those expectations.

Let me start by stating the obvious; the magnificent location lived up to the hype. We had excellent weather for 3 of our 4 days with a storm passing through one evening. Try to catch at least one sunrise, if possible. Mount Otemanu dominates the landscape; it was frequently shrouded by low-lying cloud but would not remain that way for long.

The hard product or physical plant of the resort was as expected new, contemporary, well-designed. We thoroughly enjoyed our overwater bungalow which was airy and bright. One aspect of the physical aspect of our stay was the state of the vaunted bicycles, a lack or poor distribution of the and the poor condition of the ones we could find.

Where the experience did not live up to our expectations was primarily in terms of the soft product, specifically service which turned out to be surprisingly inconsistent and even outright unwelcoming at times. Most grounds staff and housekeepers greeted us with a friendly greeting, but the same could not be said of some of their colleagues. The service during breakfast, while friendly, was hit-or-miss. The wheels truly came off the bus at the water activity center where service was poor, to put it mildly. Of 3 encounters the first was OK, the second impolite and the third almost didn't take place as staff was missing in action. It was not acceptable for a resort of this reputation and price point.

The towel rail in our bungalow came off the sink; we let the concierge know in the morning and it was fixed that afternoon. There were no corals and very few fish visible from the overwater deck despite the glass floor window.

On our second full day at the water activity center there was not even a person on station, no sign explaining when someone would return. After a while we resorted to asking at the nearby Dive Center for help; when a staffer finally arrived there was no apology, no greeting, and he was clearly unhappy at being there. I related my experience to the concierge who took notes, offered apologies, and stated the center was managed by an outside contractor. If true the Westin needs to get a new contractor or train the staff better.
review_title: Great hard product (rooms and views), but staff attitudes and attention inconsistent especially at the water center

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text: It's new, just 1 year with the Westin brand, everything looks impeccable, very fresh colors and designs, very pleasant for young people, ideal for honeymooners.

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text:
I returned from the Westin Bora Bora 1 week ago. I also stayed at the Hilton in Moorea and highly recommend both if you're doing a week in French Polynesia.

I booked the Premium Otemanu Overwater, 1 Bedroom Villa, 1 King, Premium Otemanu view, Lagoon access, Terrace and stayed in Room 258.

Overall this was the most expensive and best vacation of my life, but there were a few minor things that are just good to know before you spend all of the money.

Pros: Arrival/Departure was well organized. Resort is incredible with best view of otemanu. The upgraded room with the plunge pool was worth it and amazing. The pool and beach were also incredible. The food was excellent - I'm a vegetarian and there were plenty of healthy and tasty options for me. Breakfast at Tipanier included eggs made to order, though coffee took forever every morning. Varavara for lunch and dinner was covered by the nightly $200 credit as part of our booking. Service at restaurants and pool were good, normal good service, not overbearing. Turtle eco tour was excellent.

Good to knows: Bungalow 258 was end of pier and beautiful, but there is boat traffic coming by with people who can look into your room. The farther out your bungalow is, the deeper the water, so it wasn't really a lagoon - we didn't go in the water by the bungalow for more than a minute. The plunge pool system in our room worked just fine but there was a spouting leak. The umbrella on the deck of the room was heavy and basically can't move and doesn't tilt so for most of the day there was no shade at our room's deck. They have free bikes that are first come, first served and there are not enough bikes for everyone. They have 1 guy working 1 espresso machine at breakfast so coffee is slow. Our room was cleaned very late in the day, and 1 day it didn't get cleaned at all, though they did come for turndown service.

Con: I booked 1 tour thru the Concierge and she booked it for the wrong day so we didn't get to go on it. She said she tried to call the room to let us know, but wasn't able to reach us. The resort did not take responsibility and tried to blame it on me for booking the wrong day. Takeaway: do not use the concierge and book your excursions directly with the tour providers.
review_title: Amazing resort to experience bora bora

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text:
From what started as a dream and a goal my husband and I had 6 years ago, finally became a reality.

Our trip to Bora Bora was definitely one for the books, and thank you to The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa for exceeding every expectation. From arrival to departure, the treatment we received was exceptional. The cleanliness was top-notch, and every detail made us feel welcomed and cared for.

The service throughout the resort — from the restaurants to reception and concierge — was outstanding. Ari welcomed us like family while remaining incredibly professional. We also had amazing servers: Mana during our evenings at Tipanier and Nathalie in the mornings. Both were so kind, friendly, and attentive.

We loved every moment from beginning to end. I highly recommend the excursions and the massages as well — absolutely worth it, and something we would do all over again in a heartbeat!

100/10 experience.

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text:
I rarely leave negative reviews, but our stay at the Bora Bora Westin Marriott was incredibly disappointing and nowhere near the luxury experience we expected.

The food options at the resort were extremely limited, especially for a property at this price point. After a couple of days, there was very little variety and dining became repetitive and frustrating.

The biggest issue, however, was the condition of the room. We had multiple geckos inside the room during our stay, along with other bugs. At one point, a gecko got near our room service food and completely ruined the meal. We requested a refund for the contaminated room service order, but the resort refused -- only to be told we should have requested new food to be made.

Housekeeping and amenity checks were also severely lacking. We repeatedly found basic items missing or empty, including pool towels and body wash in the shower. After calling about the empty body wash, we waited approximately 1.5 hours before someone finally came to refill it — completely unacceptable for a luxury resort.

To make matters worse, the final bill included unexpected fees that were far higher than what Marriott originally estimated when booking. We booked using a cash + points rate, and Marriott estimated taxes and fees at 7,934 XPF per night, totaling 39,670 XPF for the stay. Instead, we were charged 61,447 XPF in taxes and fees with the only explanation being "that was an estimate" ...a nearly 55% increase in taxes and fees compared to Marriott's original estimate.

Overall, this stay was overpriced, poorly managed, and far below the standard we expect from Marriott or a Bora Bora luxury resort experience. I would not return and would strongly encourage others to look at alternative resorts before booking.
review_title: BE PREPARED TO PAY WAY MORE THAN YOUR QUOTE

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text: My husband and I went on Honeymoon and couldn't have picked a better place. The location is perfect, extremely clean everywhere, the service was impeccable and we had the best time. The food at all the restaurants was delicious and the room in the Overwater bungalow was amazing. The turtle sanctuary was an added bonus and they have great facilities. It is a very relaxed, peaceful atmosphere and worth every dollar - we definitely got our value for our money! All in all I don't think we could have had a better holiday.

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text: Highly recommend staying at the Westin Bora Bora. I stayed in the standard overwater bungalow, lagoon view, and then the premium villa Mount Otemamu view with plunge pool. Both rooms were great! Very quiet, clean, and with amazing views. The staff was very friendly and personable in trying to learn our names. Shoutout to Sebastian from guest services, and all the wonderful wait staff at Varavara and breakfast staff at Tipaniers. Food was good, but would have liked to have seen more non-seafood choices. Loved breakfast. Would love to come back one day.

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text:
Bora Bora. Even the name sounds like a promise. And the Westin delivers on that promise in almost every way imaginable.
Let's start with the views — because honestly, nothing can prepare you for them. You wake up, open your eyes, and there it is: Mount Otemanu rising majestically above a turquoise lagoon that looks photoshopped. It's not. It's just that beautiful.
The room was nothing short of spectacular. Elegant, spacious, immaculately maintained — with that mountain view as your permanent wallpaper.
And the staff — oh, the staff. These people are the true soul of this hotel. Always smiling, always genuinely helpful, always going above and beyond without being asked.
Now, I have to mention the food. Just once. Briefly. Because it deserves a mention the way a small rain cloud deserves a mention on an otherwise perfect sunny day — the Westin, for the prices charged, the cuisine somehow missed the memo that you're surrounded by some of the world's finest fresh fish, tropical fruits and incredible Polynesian culinary tradition. The restaurant feels like the one department that hasn't quite caught up with the rest of this extraordinary place.
But honestly? Book it. Go. Let the views steal your breath, let the staff spoil you rotten, and treat yourself to a local restaurant for dinner.
You won't regret a single moment.
review_title: Paradise found… just skip the restaurant.

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text:
The customer service was over the top amazing starting with our arrival and guest relations advisor. Sebastian! Not only did he take time to show us the resort he took our request for daily needs and took care of it immediately was always there for any questions or to get anything taken care of that was needed.

With breakfast buffet included in our package, we had the most amazing staff to greet us every morning by name. Fiori waitress went over and above by making a call to a restaurant manager for reservations for us at a restaurant we were planning to go to.

We felt like family there you will not be let down. You never felt crowded and always felt space.

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text: Beautiful property. Modern, tasteful finishes. Friendly and professional staff. We thoroughly enjoyed our stay. We saw a number of rays and several black tip reef sharks, just reading or relaxing on the deck of the bungalow! Breakfast buffet had tons of options – they rotated some items by the day, and you can always order eggs however you want to change it up as well. Otherwise, for food, we found it better to stick with more local cuisine (ie, fish) vs. western options (ie, we didn't find the steak or lamb that good, but it wasn't inedible either – just not something we ordered again). Yes, food is expensive, but food everywhere in Bora Bora is expensive – you're on a remote island in the middle of the south pacific! $40 for what we call a "Marriott Burger" – yes, that's a lot, but it's not that much higher than Hawaii. We didn't eat at Maere, but enjoyed the Polynesian dinner at Tipanier as well as a number of meals at Varavara and by the pool. Room service was super fast both times we used it. Ice/water machines were all over the property. We didn't find the snorkeling to be the best in Bora Bora (or diving for that matter -- other islands are better known for this) – but hard to beat that the over-water bungalow experience! We'd definitely return.
review_title: Relaxing Stay! Beautiful Property. Friendly Staff. Loved the Bungalows

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text:
Absolutely excellent in every single way. The Otemanu view OWB was perfect with a wonderful Mattress, sound system, mini fridge, Lavazza coffee maker, incredible outdoor space including plunge pool (which we loved).
The restaurants had great food (kind of spendy though, but what the heck — it's Bora Bora) and even better service.
Excursions left right from the boat dock, which was outstanding.
The best part was all of the wonderful people who work there and are just so kind and hard working.
review_title: Amazing stay for a once in a lifetime trip!

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text:
Overall a very good stay but there is some room for improvement. Having freshly opened just a few months prior to our arrival, this was one resort I had been keeping my eye on. There were speculations as to whether this would be branded a Ritz-Carlton or a W but many, including myself, were rather surprised to find it branded as a Westin.

Pre-arrival was a little patchy: there was some prolonged mix-up between payment as I had been requested to partially pre-pay around 40% of the hotel bill prior to arrival and changes in the amount to prepay a couple of times. This was not ideal but not a dealbreaker.

For the price we paid, the option of a slightly more elegant mode of transport would have been preferable — $250 round trip for 2 people for a rather small boat that is quite bumpy and crowded for only a 15-20 minute ride is rather steep.

With around 6-7 groups/couples having arrived at the resort on one boat and at times only one person manning the check-in desk, there was a bit of a queue and again not expected for a resort of this price, location and calibre. We had to wait around 25-30 minutes before even speaking to someone about checking in. We also had to wait around 4 hours before we could use our room as the previous guests were still in there.

Amenities were plentiful but a rather poorly stocked mini bar and again at this price point of over £2,000 a night, I would expect a complimentary mini bar. The outdoor area of the bungalow was also very good but a rather small pool for an almost top category room. Recent construction here means that there isn't as much wildlife as neighbouring resorts yet, and there were still some cranes up in the distance of the resort and construction going on, which was both an eyesore and an earsore at times.

Breakfast buffet was not as large as a selection I would have liked. I had specifically gone to the buffet and seen a sign for vegetarian sausages and so I placed some in my plate and ate them. Going for a second round, I saw the same sausages having been swiftly re-labelled to chicken sausages and was informed by the chef that these had been mislabelled — safe to say I was not pleased with this mishap, especially as I had informed the resort of my dietary requirements quite strictly beforehand. Food otherwise was good, dessert was a standout, but there was not much variety between nights at Tipanier.

Other facilities including the gym was rather small for a Westin. I did not go to the spa as the price for 2 of us to have an hours spa felt rather exorbitant at an all in cost of nearly £400.

In summary, Bora Bora truly lives up to its reputation and is a piece of paradise on Earth, making us overlook other less positive aspects of the resort. There is certainly some need for further staff training, and the food and dining experience require urgent attention. Would we return? Yes, provided some minor hiccups are rectified.
review_title: Should have been branded a W

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text:
After a long and tiring journey through Australia and New Zealand, we ended our holidays by relaxing for 10 days in Bora Bora. For our stay, we chose the recently opened The Westin Bora Bora. The facilities are new and well maintained. Yes, this is one of the most stunningly beautiful destinations we have encountered in our many travels—but also one of the most expensive.

Upon arrival we were welcomed with Polynesian tiare flower garlands and check-in was handled in a friendly and efficient manner. We received an upgrade to a Premium Overwater Villa with a pool.

The room was spacious. The king-sized bed had a comfortable mattress, but the duvet was too warm and heavy, and the blanket provided was too short. The range of toiletries was of average quality and somewhat limited; on a few occasions, we had to request shower gel. There was plenty of coffee and tea in the room, but no bottled water — instead water had to be collected by ourselves from designated stations. The villa had a deck with sun loungers and a small pool, with a stunning view of Mount Otemanu — this is where we spent most of our stay. The outdoor volume from speakers should be limited, as we had neighbors whose music was too loud and had to be asked to turn it down.

The daily breakfast buffet at Tipanier was good but did not particularly impress; flies were a major inconvenience at the buffet. For dinner, we tried all the restaurants (Varavara, Tipanier, and Maere), but honestly, none of the meals stood out, and prices were high. It is worth emphasizing that all the staff who served us were outstanding, though one of the bartenders, although hardworking and kind, needed more training: on two occasions he spilled the daiquiris we ordered on us.

In summary, Bora Bora truly lives up to its reputation and is a piece of paradise on Earth, making us overlook other less positive aspects of the resort. The property's infrastructure is luxurious, more so than its amenities. There is certainly some need for further staff training, and the food and dining experience require urgent attention. Our final rating would be 4.5… however, the idyllic setting easily leads us to give it 5 stars on TripAdvisor!
review_title: Bora Bora: a must do before dying!…

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text: Our stay at The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa was absolutely unforgettable. We stayed in a Mount Otemanu View Villa, and it exceeded every expectation. The villa itself was stunning: modern, spotless, beautifully designed. One feature we especially loved was the Bluetooth speaker system. The service throughout our stay was exceptional. Dining was also fantastic, with our favorite restaurant being Varavara. We also loved the provided bikes. If you're considering staying here, do it.

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text: Great experience. The resort is beautiful and in great shape. We had a slight issue at check in, but the GM responded quickly and handled it to satisfaction. Our room was in great shape and very clean, highly recommend a villa with pool!
review_title: Great stay! Cant wait to return

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text:
We were a little worried before checking in due to the mixed reviews and the fact that the resort had only recently reopened. But our actual experience turned out to be fantastic — easily the best among all the 5-star hotels we stayed at on this trip.

1. Exceptional location — the setting is unbeatable, with what I'd consider the best, most direct view of the mountain.
2. Newly updated, modern rooms — all the rooms have been fully refreshed. The pool villas with mountain views are especially worth it.
3. Food exceeded expectations — contrary to some older reviews, we found the food to be genuinely good, and the pricing is more reasonable than other 5-star properties in Bora Bora.
4. Thoughtful touches — the reusable water bottle gift was one of the highlights of our stay.

Overall, the Westin Bora Bora far exceeded our expectations. We would absolutely return.
review_title: Stunning Views, Modern Rooms, and Surprisingly Great Food

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text: We stayed 7 nights at the Westin in February, one of the most beautiful places Ive ever been. Both the resort and the scenery. Counting the days until we can return!

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text:
From the airport to the resort was a breeze. We were greeted by staff members while one of the male staff members was singing and strumming his ukulele during docking. Checking in was a bit of a wait, but it's no fault of Westin, our arrival time was early. The resort is very well kept and clean. The villa was roomy, nothing too extravagant or jaw dropping, but the view beyond the deck was stunning.

Our experience with Westin's staff were all very hospitable and professional. Memorable staff members that left an etch in me was Iona, Mana, and the activity guy.

For every goodness there is always a BUT. For the price that Westin is charging to stay per night, one would think that the mini bar in their room would be stocked full of sodas, bottled water, and/or alcohol. Instead, it's an empty mini fridge with nothing in it. The "gift" (a stainless water container) was a means for the customer to refill their own water if they wanted filtered water. No complimentary bottled water, sodas, or snacks. Six cans of sodas on the main island is $12 and one can of soda on the resort is $9. We're not going for nickels and dimes, but arms and legs.

The food was okay the first night and maybe second. Anything after the third night, everything went from okay to mediocre. Nothing authentic. I remember talking to a fellow vacationer about the food at the resort and that person felt exactly how I felt.

Overall, our experience with the Polynesian people was pleasant. Our stay at Westin was pleasant as well. Westin just need to reach in a lot deeper to provide the little things for their customers instead of keep reaching in a lot deeper to get out of their customers.

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text: We stayed 6 days at the resort with our five year old daughter and absolutely loved it! It truly is paradise there! The icing on the cake is the Eco Center which rescues turtles, so you are also doing good! The staff is amazing. Too many to name them all but some shout outs to Hamdi, the manager of the rooms; Arthur, our wonderful guest relations manager; Mana, the head waiter; Sarah, the restaurant manager; Lucie, the food and beverage manager and the lovely waiters loana and Heifara! They all made sure that we received a very tailored and customised experience. We had a villa facing Mount Otemanu, which I highly recommend. We hope to be back soon!
review_title: Fantastic family holiday + turtle eco center

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text: An extremely disappointing hotel with the aesthetic of an American airport lounge planted in one of the most beautiful islands on earth. Vast empty charmless spaces, overly designed rooms again with that business centre decor imposed within a faux Tahitian bungalow layout. Awful bathroom fixtures straight out of the ‘Leroy Merlin’ catalogue. Harsh white lighting, adjustable, but complex and cold. Aside from the above the hotel is grossly overpriced for what it is at core… a standard westin…and the staff whilst courteous and pleasant are over reliant on training and lack the sort of spontaneous warmth which is so much a part of these islands. They simply respond according to their rule book and roll eyes with irritation if taken off script. By the way if you book on booking.com expect to be asked for full payment for the entire duration of your stay when you check in, including service charge for services you have not yet had (plus a separate payment retention for extras). You will also be asked to sign an extensive rule ‘manifesto’ of perhaps 2000 small print obligations before you are allowed to check in. These include a 500 euro fine for smoking even in outside spaces, such as on the terrace you just prepaid. And generally your idea of paradise is IKEA with a view, it’s for you. If not, I suggest you find your happiness elsewhere.
review_title: Overpriced characterless, perfect for Americans. Eyes rolling staff.

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text: I am giving this resort 4 stars because everything else, the location, amenities, excursions, and service, is genuinely excellent. However, the food situation is serious and it has to be mentioned. You cannot simply leave the resort to eat elsewhere, so you are committed to eating at the resort. Most dining options are significantly overpriced for the poor quality provided. The Tipanier Polynesian Dinner & Show was the biggest disappointment of our entire trip, in our opinion a complete waste of 380 USD. The Varavara restaurant was a similarly poor experience. When we raised our concerns, management sat down with us personally, listened carefully, took notes, and acknowledged they are aware of the pattern about food being mentioned in some reviews. They told us they are currently working on a major restructure of their food service to improve quality. Breakfast buffet is actually good. Lunch: skip the restaurants entirely. Dinner: book Maere in advance, food is genuinely good there.
review_title: Stunning Resort with One Major Issue that Management Seems to be Actively Addressing

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text: We just got home from a fabulous week stay at the Westin. We stayed at this resort when it was le Meridian a few years back and we thought it was great then. The new makeover looks awesome. Very modern. We loved the morning breakfasts and the dinner meals. We also signed up for a few of the free activities which were very fun. This resort has a nice gym that we used daily. Our room (328) was super nice. We had a casita facing the mountain with a pool. Our room was the best part of our stay. I only wish there were more bikes to use since we had friends on the opposite wing of the dock so it was a long walk to visit them. The spa was great. We did a couples massage and it was very relaxing 10 out 10. The staff members are so nice and remember your names when you see them each day. We loved this resort and we will be back.

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text: Bora Bora is a dream and our second time going. The first time we stayed at a different resort and had a fantastic experience. This time we stayed at the Westin because we are loyal Marriott BonVoy members. The staff lovely, the resort only two years old after remodeling and very nice. The problem we had was the food. We purchased the package with daily breakfast and dinner which was the wrong decision. There are 4 restaurants and the pool bar but unfortunately they all have the exact same menu. No variety and most of the food was very bland, even the fruit which was surprising. We always told them tapwater but they would open bottled water instead and pour it before we could say no. At check out they tried to charge us for bottled water but took it off. We were given a thermos at check in to fill with tap water, but the water tasted moldy. It was disgusting. So for the food and lack of variety alone, we would recommend going to a different resort.
review_title: Other resorts have much better food and better variety.

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text: Excellent resort. From the time we arrived at Bora Bora airport, we felt taken care of. Resort was beautiful. Plenty of outdoor seating whether at the pool or the beach. The overwater bungalow was excellent. The mini fridge was a nice perk. Very friendly staff. The kayaks & SUP’s were great. Sunscreen located around the property. Was given a water bottle upon arrival and there are water/ice stations throughout. Great to see the turtle sanctuary.

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text: The Westin is the newest resort in Bora Bora. It is beautiful and comfortable and simply amazing. We felt so welcomed upon arrival. We stayed over the water. The villa was new and spacious. Very cold air conditioning and a wonderful bed. The pool/beach are amazing. The restaurants were good. There was a special Valentine's Day dinner that we attended and it was delicious! And breakfast was always good. I had a wonderful massage and facial at the spa. Room service was also fast and delicious. We highly recommend the Westin and The St. Regis on Bora Bora!

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text: Westin did it right. There are a few areas they could improve but overall one the best resorts we've stayed at. The Front desk manager / Director of Reception, Hamdi, was very condescending. Rude! He did not make for a good arrival impression. Hamdi chose not to extend the free breakfast to both of our villas even though both my husband and myself are Titanium Marriott members. He was also not knowledgeable regarding the resort. Other than Hamdi and our issues at check in, our stay was fantastic! We loved the OWB with pool. Turn down service was sparatic/hit or miss across nights. The section of glass in the floor already showed scratches. We were told there were bikes to get from place to place but we could find only 4 bikes on the resort and they had rusted chains, broken spokes, stuck brakes. We had to call a cart and would wait 15-30 minutes, sometimes they never showed making us late for an excursion. We had an issue with the shower flooding and water bubbling up in the tub and sinks with an overflow system; notified them, they came to look, but it never got fixed. We had reservations for flower crown making, but not enough crowns or flowers for everyone. On a pearl diving excursion I got stung by what the guide said were baby jellyfish and he was not surprised or sympathetic, offered no aid. Blandine the Guest services manager and the concierge team (Hinatea, Aubrey) were superb.

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text: We spent 5 nights at the Westin Bora Bora and couldn't have enjoyed it more. The resort itself is gorgeous, with first-class accommodations (we had an overwater bungalow with a plunge pool), fantastic food, and beautiful landscaping. We didn't have a single meal we didn't love and the menus had a lot of variety. Every member of the staff we encountered greeted us warmly and were endlessly helpful. Special thanks to Arthur, Heitiare, and Ariivai the concierge. If you have an overwater room, be sure to leave your water light on at night - we saw sea turtles, stingrays, and so many different kinds of fish. Everything about our experience was magical.

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text: We stayed at the Westin for Valentines and I was shocked at how nice it was. The rooms were clean, the AC worked great, all of what we expected and more. Being able to ride bikes around the property was awesome. We went to their dinner restaurant Maere twice and we had Maxime both nights who was awesome, always ready to get me another tropical ice tea or a bucket of ice! We are already thinking of going back!

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text: The Westin Bora Bora runs like other Westins. Efficiently, effectively and precisely. The location is the only exception - if you weren't in an overwater bungalow you'd think you were at any other Westin property. We initially requested an overwater bungalow and were brought to rm 247, at the apex of all the golf cart traffic (not quiet) and unimpressive - small and crowded feeling. The next day we requested a move and at an obnoxious cost, we were upgraded to an overwater bungalow with pool and view - significantly larger, more private, but deeper water with a lot of boat traffic and wake. Housekeeping and laundry were great though expensive. Restaurants all 'ok' - breakfast buffet gets tired after the same selection every day. You will have sticker shock unless you're made of money - water, snacks, everything is very expensive, nothing in the bar fridge.
review_title: Meh. Nothing to write home about.

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text: We stayed something like 55 nights at Conrad, 5 at St.Regis over the years. Conrad cancelled on us due to renovations so I picked 10 nights at Westin, formerly Le Meridien, fully renovated and reopened under new brand. It's a very well-run hotel, same owner as Conrad. Westin has the big advantage over Conrad of straight views of the iconic Mt Otemanu; our upgrade as Bonvoy Ambassador Elite gave us a larger overwater villa, unobstructed mountain view, and a plunge pool - the trifecta. The glass floor is a big plus at Westin, lacking at Conrad. However Westin has some features inferior to Conrad such as less inspirational dining, and the water near Westin/St.Regis/InterContinental/Four Seasons is a bit more cloudy than at Conrad because Conrad gets fresh water straight from the ocean. Overall we liked our stay enough that I can see splitting future stays between Westin and Conrad.
review_title: The Latest and Greatest Resort in Bora Bora

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text: Unbelievably beautiful. This is where I will try to go instead of Hawaii. Was worried about January being in the rainy season but weather was gorgeous. The Westin is very nice, but I don't think you could go wrong with the other big 3 or 4 chains. Will definitely go back, but will also visit Moorea or similar islands.

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text: This has been the best vacation of our lives. The place itself is magical, and the team and staff are simply exceptional. At every position in the hotel, employees are professional but also super pleasant, smiling and warm. Thanks to Maxime in particular. A big thank you to Lucile also who managed to organize a unique and magical marriage proposal despite the weather constraints. The food was excellent and we feasted from start to finish.
review_title: The best hotel experience of my life!

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text: We stayed one night in this hotel, only luxury, friendly staff, very good table, a bungalow on the lagoon. Few fish in the lagoon. Room price varies between 1200 and 1600 euros per night. You have to have a big budget to stay there.
review_title: Luxury hotel, apparently the cheapest atoll

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text: We had a wonderful stay at the Westin Bora Bora. Rooms are recently renovated and thoughtfully designed, staff were welcoming and helpful - special mention to Arthur, Blandine, and Florie. The twice daily housekeeping was great. A few small suggestions: more bikes scattered around the property, more fans at the restaurants to keep cool, and some shade over parts of the pool would all be lovely. We were initially supposed to split time between the Conrad and the Westin; the Conrad cancelled our reservation (very stressful) as they undergo renovations. It worked out - we were thrilled with the Westin and will return here instead of the Conrad/soon-to-be Waldorf Astoria.

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text: We stayed at this hotel for three nights and enjoyed every second of it. Every detail is well thought out from airport pickup with cold water, to the cart ride with ukulele player, to check-out and boat ride back to the airport. Everything ran seamlessly the entire time we were there. I would highly recommend this hotel and would stay here again without hesitation.

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text: This hotel is incredible! It feels brand new, has spectacular views. We stayed in overwater bungalow #212, very well appointed and comfortable. The staff here were fantastic, every interaction was thoughtfully executed. We especially loved Thierry at the pool bar. The breakfast restaurant was closed for dinner during our stay. Overall the food and drinks are pricey ($30-50 per plate & $30 for cocktails/wine) but quality, taste and portions are great. I highly recommend buying the breakfast package as it was about $150 per day for two without it.

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text: Relatively new hotel, so everything was very nice, rooms are beautiful and in good condition, though bikes are already tired out and creaky - the salty water and humidity kills them fast. The location is perfect, lush greenery and lot of colorful flowers; the view towards the mountain is the most dramatic of the whole island. People are very nice everywhere. There are some activities, but after 8pm there is not much to do. Hotel is pricey, but compared to other similar hotels, better value.

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text: A very nice and well maintained complex. The staff exudes a natural friendliness and is very attentive and helpful. On our departure to Papeete I left my camera in our room. Since the GM had an appointment there two days later, he was so nice and delivered them to me personally.

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text: Stayed at the Westin Bora Bora for our honeymoon for 6 nights. Spectacular location and our room was beautiful but it was all down hill after that. The food was average at best and ridiculously over priced, even when we returned some food to the kitchen it came out terrible again. There appeared to be constant confusion amongst the staff even from some of the hotel managers. The service in the restaurants was appalling - we asked for items that never appeared so we just left and gave up. No mini bar stocked on arrival or replenished unless requested; we had to order room service to stock the bar at additional cost. We almost fell over when on our last day we found out our food and drink bill came to over $6000 AUD! We did not eat or drink excessively. Would not return, absolute worst value for money of any holiday I have been on - so disappointing when it was our honeymoon and we spent over $20000 AUD to stay there. Tried to feedback to hotel chain and was offered an apology and $100 credit in hotel points.

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text: An unforgettable stay at Westin Bora Bora. We stayed as a couple and everything exceeded our expectations: the setting, absolutely paradisiacal, the magnificent facilities and an atmosphere at the same time luxurious, soothing and cocooning. A huge thank you to the staff - special mention to Alan the beach attendant, Jasmina the bartender, and Noémie my masseuse. Every detail is designed to make you feel privileged. We leave with magical memories.

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text: We just departed the newly renovated Westin Bora Bora. Beautiful design paired with generally good service, amenities are quite nice. The Polynesian dinner on Thursday was a highlight, as was the morning breakfast buffet. The remainder of our dining experiences felt adequate and somewhat overpriced for the quality. Recommendations: adding ceiling fans in 'O'a Bar, offering evening turndown service, and addressing the boat transfer back to the airport - the motor on our transfer boat was clearly malfunctioning and required everyone to cover their ears, which was concerning.

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text: We came on our honeymoon and also for my partner's birthday. Beautifully renovated and thoughtfully designed, which is why I gave this three stars, but the execution left something to be desired. We came during the off season and the entire resort was understaffed - breakfast orders kept being forgotten, food would take ages, basic things like water or condiments would run out frequently. In room service would call you back 20 minutes later just to take your order, then arrive 45 minutes later cold. 15-30 minute wait for a cart. Every bike is rusty with flat tires and broken handles/brakes. They ran out of snorkeling gear entirely. The 'fancy' restaurant's food is nearly inedible unless it's Polynesian; their 'Italian' menu was as if they followed an AI recipe. They also forgot my partner's birthday despite being reminded during dinner. No do-not-disturb sign - staff would appear at odd hours constantly ringing the bell. The Westin needs better training, more staff, and more management in order to succeed - don't expect a five star experience here.
review_title: Beautiful resort that needs more staff and structure to make it great

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text: Third time staying with family on this property - 2000, 2009 and 2025. The major renovation is very impressive. Service from pickup at airport to drop off was top notch. Mixed drinks could be better. Expensive - USD 30 per mai tai - but you know that going in. We were here during Xmas week and definitely encountered the rainy season element. Snorkeling isn't good on the property, no change from past - snorkeling at the reef south side of island is great. We rented a pontoon boat from La Plage - worth it to see eagle rays, sting rays. Thumbs up to the management of this property.

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text: A friend and I stayed 21-25 December 2025. We absolutely loved our time here. Every staff person we interacted with was extremely friendly and accommodating. Highlights: the beaches and water were sublime, the everyday breakfast buffet was incredible especially for Christmas, the Eco Center was a real treat, the spa was delightful, Santa Claus landed on the beach via water ski and it was the best Santa arrival I've ever seen.
review_title: Magical Four-Night Stay with a Friend

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text: This is a beautiful hotel, recent renovations superbly done, rooms chic and extremely comfortable. The Westin may have a bit less sophistication than the Four Seasons or a couple of the other hotels on Bora Bora but the staff is incredibly friendly. That said, we are here at Christmas and the rates are SKY HIGH - dinner on Christmas Eve was a set price of $350 per person, excluding booze. Once you are here, you are captive and have to deal with it. We've also had a ton of rain which is no fault of the hotel.

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text: Paradise, there is no other way to describe. Service was amazing from the time we landed at the airport. Restaurants and room service were fantastic. The overwater bungalows were beyond anything we could have imagined. I could not imagine what more the St. Regis and Four Seasons could offer to make someone want to stay there for double the cost. There is no better deal. Get here before they realize they can charge twice as much.
review_title: Best resort I have ever been to.

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text: Our stay was everything we had hoped for. From the greeting at the airport to our flawless check-in, everything told me we found our vacation spot. We decided to celebrate our 25th anniversary in Bora Bora. Our overwater bungalow with a plunge pool was stunning. I have some balance issues which prohibits me from riding a bike and was concerned that would be an issue - it was not, as we would call for a cart pickup and it always arrived promptly. We ate in each restaurant and found the food to be varied, tasty and excellent, the wine list superb. I highly recommend this property.
review_title: Absolutely Stunning Stay at the Westin Bora Bora

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text: We had a wonderful stay at The Westin Bora Bora, the resort is beautiful, relaxing, and impeccably maintained. The service truly stood out, especially thanks to Matthew who went above and beyond to make our experience smooth and memorable. As well as to Moeata and her attention to detail in the restaurant.

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text: Lovely property on atoll, they pick you up and bring you back to airport by boat. However, there is music almost everywhere on the property, by the pool, the beach, the bar, reception, hard to get away from the music - and it is not usually Tahitian music, but American pop (a lot of souped up Christmas music too). Be prepared for everything additional to be super expensive. Staff are super friendly. There is the start of a coral garden in the small lagoon but a few fish, not many, so don't expect a super snorkeling experience from the beach. There were a couple of power outages, not confined to the resort, also on the main island.

hotel: The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa
review_text: Unfortunately, this was not a hotel I would ever go back and stay. We had to wait 3 hours past check-in. When we finally got our rooms, neither key worked. I started to unpack in the closet and a leak started in the light fixture - water came gushing out on me and some of my clothes; no one offered to clean any of my clothes. There really isn't any privacy on the back deck - a neighbor's teenage son would not stop jumping from the deck into the water at sunset and woke us up multiple mornings at 7:30.
